hero.headline: Second student comes forward in St. Lucie County school bus driver molestation case
hero.body:
A second alleged victim has come forward in the case against a St. Lucie County school bus driver arrested on lewd and lascivious molestation charges. The bus driver was initially arrested after the first student made allegations, and authorities now say a second student has reported similar incidents.

The arrest follows an investigation by St. Lucie County authorities into allegations involving students who rode on the bus driven by the accused. The school bus driver faces charges related to both alleged victims.

Parents and guardians of students in St. Lucie County are being urged to speak with their children if they rode buses driven by the accused. Authorities are asking anyone with information about the case to contact the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. School district officials are cooperating with the ongoing investigation.

The case remains under active investigation as prosecutors review the evidence and additional charges may be filed. The school bus driver is currently in custody. Parents with concerns about their children's safety on school buses can contact St. Lucie County School District transportation officials for information about routes and driver assignments.

Drivers are urged to seek alternate routes while crews work to clear the scene. No information has been released yet about injuries or when the lanes will reopen. Motorists should expect significant delays in the area.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie daughter charged with attempted murder and arson after setting bedroom fire
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman faces attempted murder and arson charges after allegedly setting fire to her mother's bedroom while her mother was inside. Michelle Picard, 26, was arrested following an investigation into a house fire in Port St. Lucie.

The victim first noticed smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door. When she opened the door, she discovered Picard standing nearby. Investigators determined that Picard had deliberately set the fire while her mother was in the room, leading to the attempted murder charge in addition to arson.

The fire displaced the victim from her home. Port St. Lucie police conducted the investigation that led to Picard's arrest. The case remains under investigation as prosecutors prepare charges.

Residents with information about the incident are encouraged to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department. The investigation continues as authorities work to determine the full circumstances surrounding the fire and what led to the alleged attack.

cards.headline: Downtown Fort Pierce visitors now face hefty fines for parking over 2 hours

The new enforcement policy targets vehicles that exceed the posted two-hour time limits in downtown parking areas. Citations carry hefty fines for violators who overstay the allowed parking duration. The change impacts anyone visiting downtown Fort Pierce for extended shopping trips, dining, or business appointments.

The stricter parking enforcement comes as Fort Pierce works to manage parking availability in its downtown commercial district. Business owners and customers who regularly visit the area will need to monitor their parking times closely to avoid fines. The policy applies to public parking spaces with posted time restrictions throughout the downtown area.

Downtown Fort Pierce stakeholders will need to adjust their parking habits under the new enforcement regime. Visitors planning extended stays in the downtown district may need to move their vehicles or find alternative parking arrangements to comply with the two-hour limits and avoid citations.

cards.body:

The levee upgrade provides long-awaited flood protection for a community that has lived with fears of rising water for years. Residents endured significant flooding during Tropical Storm Isaac, which damaged homes and left some trapped by floodwaters. The completed levee system now offers protection against future storms.

The new Jupiter Fire Rescue department will provide fire protection and emergency services directly operated by the town. Previously, Jupiter relied on contracted or county fire services. The 91 sworn firefighters will now serve Jupiter residents through the new municipal department.

Vero Beach continues to attract relocating professionals from northeastern states who seek year-round warm weather and beach access.

hero.headline: Florida sues OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman over concealed ChatGPT safety risks
hero.body:
Florida has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman, accusing the artificial intelligence company of hiding serious risks associated with ChatGPT from users. The state claims OpenAI prioritized profits over safety and knowingly allowed the chatbot technology to cause harm to Floridians.

The lawsuit alleges that OpenAI concealed the dangerous capabilities of ChatGPT and failed to warn users about potential risks. Florida argues that the company knew its product would cause harm but released it anyway. According to the legal filing, the state claims ChatGPT aided and abetted mass shooters, with OpenAI allowing the technology to provide assistance in planning or executing violent attacks.

The legal action targets both the San Francisco-based company and Altman personally, holding leadership accountable for decisions regarding ChatGPT's deployment. Florida contends that OpenAI executives were aware of the serious safety concerns but chose to move forward with public release of the technology without adequate safeguards or disclosures to protect users and the public.

The lawsuit represents a significant challenge to one of the leading artificial intelligence companies as states grapple with regulating rapidly advancing AI technologies. Florida's legal action could set precedent for how states hold AI companies accountable for harms caused by their products. The case raises questions about corporate responsibility in the AI industry and what disclosures companies must make about potential dangers associated with their technologies. OpenAI has not yet publicly responded to the Florida lawsuit.

cards.headline: President Trump nominates Florida House Speaker Daniel Perez as ambassador to Brazil
cards.teaser: The Florida House Speaker has been tapped for a diplomatic post in South America.
cards.body:

The nomination moves Perez from state legislative leadership to a potential role in international diplomacy representing American interests in the largest South American nation.

The nomination requires Senate confirmation before Perez can assume the ambassadorial position. If confirmed, Perez would leave his role leading the Florida House of Representatives, potentially triggering a leadership transition in Tallahassee as legislators would need to select a new speaker.

The policy divergence comes as Florida itself has filed a major lawsuit against OpenAI over ChatGPT safety concerns. Donalds' stance on AI could become a significant issue in the gubernatorial campaign as Florida voters and legislators debate how the state should approach regulating rapidly advancing artificial intelligence technologies.
